criteria.accounted_chunks: Permit final JavaScript to keep static import edges only when every edge target is a file listed in the published bundle manifest with a verified digest; keep rejecting dynamic import, require calls, native, absolute and remote edges unconditionally.
criteria.hermetic_bundle: Require the final published JavaScript to be fully self contained: reject every static or dynamic import edge in bundled output, since the single-entry browser build is expected to inline all reachable code into one file.

bundle_edge_rule.instructions: Which import-edge rule should the post-bundle audit enforce on published browser JavaScript?

criteria.traverse_all: Traverse every declared edge including import type and export type re-exports when computing reachability, and inspect the bodies of all modules reached either way, because any reachable file could still carry executable content the auditor has not seen.
criteria.values_only: Verify type-only edges are declared and resolve, but traverse only value-carrying edges for reachability and body inspection, because import type and export type edges are erased deterministically before bundling and cannot execute.

reachability_edges.instructions: Should type-only TypeScript edges extend audit reachability or only be checked for declaration?

criteria.grandfather_emission: Accept the host operations and native edges reachable from current browser emission as a pinned baseline, and reject only violations that do not appear in that baseline, so the existing build keeps passing while new leaks are caught.
criteria.strict_fail_closed: Reject every reachable host operation, native edge and server-only module in the audited graph, even where current browser emission trips the rule, and leave emission repair to the later pruning and browser-operation tasks that own those files.

strictness_posture.instructions: When the current browser emission reaches real host operations, should the new audit fail or pin a baseline?

state.baseline: Today the state module of a browser generation imports platform/log.ts, whose default host calls Bun.write, plus platform/io.ts with a node:util edge, platform/markdown.ts calling Bun.markdown.html, and further Bun uses in clock, assets, html, cookies and csrf helpers. The http chain also reaches assert/context.ts, whose identity helper imports node:crypto. None of this is quoted string data; it is executable host access reachable from the browser root.
state.mandate: Can has zero external users and no backwards-compatibility obligation. Task UP10 must replace the raw-substring browser audit with structural resolution of all generated, dependency and runtime imports and host operations, supplying pre-bundle graph and post-bundle bundle/map/table audit interfaces to the later bundling task. Finding B01 demands that quoted Bun., node: introduction and require( data pass while actual forbidden operations fail, that runtime bodies cannot escape inspection, and that the auditor never relies on a bundler silently removing forbidden reachable code.
state.pipeline: UP10 owns only the auditor. Emission pruning by reachability belongs to the later compiler task UP11, browser operation adapters to UP13, and verified Bun.build bundling with the sealed runtime overlay and content manifest to UP15. The auditor defines the pass/fail boundary those tasks build against; it cannot edit their files.
state.type_edges: The sealed browser profile keeps runtime/completion.ts, whose first line is export type { AssertionContext } from ./assert/context.ts. That edge is erased before execution, while other assert/context.ts edges, such as the denyLiveBoundary value import in platform/http.ts, are live value edges.
